rows.name: Own margin error vs rest differential
rows.note: A positive value means the model under-predicts the home team when the home team has had more rest.

rows.name: Own total error vs rest differential
rows.note: Tests whether scoring totals react to rest in a way the model does not capture.

rows.name: Own predicted margin vs the market spread
rows.note: How strongly the own model agrees with the third-party closing line.

rows.name: Own margin error vs the size of the actual margin
rows.note: A negative value means the model over-predicts the favourite: it over-states the margin of large favourites and under-states the margin of large underdogs.

rows.name: Same-week parlay leg dependence (cover rate lift)
rows.note: Joint rate at which two different games in the same week both cover, divided by the product of the two marginal cover rates. 1.00 means the legs are independent and a parlay prices as the product. Values above 1.00 mean parlays pay less than the product of the singles.

rows.name: Same-game ATS and total joint hit rate
rows.scope: 1999-2026, every game with both a spread and a total
rows.note: The joint rate at which the home side covers the spread and the game also goes over the total. This is the dependence a same-game parlay has to price; the product of the two marginal rates is the independent assumption.

rows.name: Product of the marginal same-game rates
rows.note: The independent assumption for CR-06. Comparing CR-06 with CR-07 gives the same-game dependence.

rows.name: Carried-in offensive rating vs 2026 points scored
rows.note: The rating a team carried into the 2026 season against the points it actually scored in 2026. The rating was fitted on 2025 and earlier results, so this is an out-of-sample test of the rating.

rows.name: Carried-in defensive rating vs 2026 points conceded
rows.note: The defence's rating carried into the 2026 season against the points it actually conceded in 2026.

rows.name: Own predicted total vs actual total
rows.note: Fit of the own scoring model on the holdout.

rows.name: Own win probability vs home-win outcome
rows.note: For a perfectly calibrated model this correlation equals the square root of the base rate times one minus the base rate, which here is 0.500. A value well below that reference means the model is under-confident: its probabilities sit too close to one half. See the calibration table on the Own Lines page.

note: Correlations marked third-party in scope use the archive's closing lines. Correlations computed on model errors use only the own model and the official final scores.
